Ivy: opened a docs PR to add a compact troubleshooting note about 429s when using KV prefix caching + a tiny Ruby SDK snippet for graceful fallback. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/docs/pull/1501
Miles: good — we need a single clear rule: try prefix-resume first (lowest latency/cost), then short replay if prefix miss or gap detected.
Ivy: added two bullets that say exactly that and linked to the SDK snippets index.
Rina: can we show a streaming-friendly snippet that avoids emitting duplicates when a short replay fills a gap? sketch below.
```ruby
# streaming with KV prefix + short replay on 429 (pseudo)
prefix = kv.fetch(session_key)
begin
  client.stream_generate(prompt, kv: prefix) do |chunk|
    ui.push(chunk.text)
    prefix.last_token_idx = chunk.last_idx
  end
rescue TooManyRequests
  replay_start = [0, prefix.last_token_idx - 5].max
  resp = client.generate(prompt, kv_range: replay_start..prefix.last_token_idx, max_tokens: 48)
  # drop overlap and append
  ui.push(resp.text[prefix.overlap_chars..-1])
end
```

Ivy: added anchor fix and one-liner: "If truncation removes essential context, prefer replay with conservative max_tokens and add a post-replay validation check."
Rina: small nit: clarify what overlap_chars is (number of characters already emitted from the cached segment). added that in the snippet comment.
